title: Joseph’s Brothers Didn’t Just Hate Him—They Planned Murder
paragraphs: Joseph’s Brothers Didn’t Just Hate Him—They Planned Murder
They smiled at the table.
But their hearts were already sharpening knives.
Joseph walked into the field wearing the coat his father gave him, not knowing the men watching him were not just annoyed…
They were ready to erase him.
“Come now therefore, and let us slay him… and we shall see what will become of his dreams.” — Genesis 37:20
Read that again.
They didn’t just hate Joseph.
They hated what God showed him.
But here’s what most people don’t realize…
Sometimes the people closest to you don’t hate your weakness.
They hate the evidence that God’s hand is on you.
God saw it.

The jealousy.
The whispers.
The fake concern.
The moment love turned into violence.
And Joseph?
He was thrown into a pit.

No water.
No rescue.
No explanation.
Just betrayal echoing off the walls.
You knew what that felt like.

To be misunderstood.
Rejected.
Punished for something God placed inside you.
But Joseph’s pit was not the end.
It was the road.
Because what his brothers meant for evil, God was already bending toward redemption.
“Ye thought evil against me; but God meant it unto good.” — Genesis 50:20
That is not prosperity talk.
That is providence.

Joseph suffered.
Joseph was sold.
Joseph was forgotten.
But God was writing something bigger than revenge.
And this points us to Jesus.

Rejected by His own.
Betrayed for silver.
Condemned by jealous men.
Thrown into death itself.
But the cross was not defeat.
It was redemption.
“Christ Jesus came into the world to save sinners.” — 1 Timothy 1:15
Your enemies cannot cancel God’s purpose.
But your bitterness can poison your soul.

Repent.
Forgive.
Trust Christ.
Let God judge what wounded you.
Originally written by Gospel Warrior.
